acknowledged_prior_outcomes: PR251 showed calibration for 8 distance×season×phase detector q and 4 season×phase near-passage mix w; PR253 found fixed-table oracle strong interaction tipping radius delta≈0.13589. Neither is an equal-total-reference-opportunity resource allocation trial.
question: At the SAME total externally labeled true passage opportunity count, should ecology field effort prioritize calibrating detector q(distance,season,solar bin) or independently measuring target near/far passage mix w(season,solar bin), to certify an actual within-site seasonal encounter timing OR after astronomical normalization?
observation_frame: For every strategy, 8 independent q reference cells (2 distance classes×4 branch×solar-bin) each have q_n independent gold-standard passages. Four target mix cells each have w_n independently labeled true passage opportunities. Equal cost is exactly 8*q_n+4*w_n at each listed budget, not equal animal detections.

alpha.q_CI: eight two-sided Bonferroni Clopper–Pearson intervals each one-sided tail 0.0125/16
alpha.w_CI: four two-sided Bonferroni Clopper–Pearson intervals each one-sided tail 0.0125/8
alpha.animal_test: fixed-season and time-bin margins noncentral Fisher P_null(X>=x) at max detector crossproduct B times documented effort OR

synthetic_sampling.q_reference_successes: eight independent binomial(q_n,q_stratum), never chosen based on focal detector outcomes
synthetic_sampling.w_target_successes: four independent binomial(w_n,w_target), independently labeled from all actual passages including missed focal detector events
synthetic_sampling.animal_observed_counts: independent draw from Fisher noncentral hypergeometric at theta_latent*target_detector_gamma, conditioned upon each frozen 2x2 animal margin

metrics: all 4 truths×4 total budgets×3 strategies×200 full draws
robust certification fraction and binomial Monte Carlo standard error
4-reference-q, 4-target-w joint coverage separately and all 12 cells coverage
HOLD where detector denominator lower interval includes 0
median finite conservative detector seasonal crossproduct bound B
oracle conditional test rate with true detector crossproduct known, reported as diagnostic not a fair equal-cost field technique
paired best strategy within each fixed budget determined ONLY after scoring; no posthoc candidate additions

each strategy actual external opportunity count equals fixed total budget
calibration samples independent of animal detections and each other, all near/far mixes based on opportunities not detected photos
all gamma(qeff) envelopes calculated by exact corner extrema
under calibration failure alpha bounds and exact test null, union bound mathematically <=.05; Monte Carlo observed frequencies are not the formal guarantee
one-sided Fisher null conditional calibration fixed at alpha=.025
include all negative and null worlds, no conditioning on significant results
original 41 astronomical dates and earlier first-results ledger untouched
original EcoBank v1.1 archive, actual camera logs, independent detector reference and animal events unverified/unopened

claim_boundary: One physical site and one fixed 2-bin matched photoperiod comparison with reference gold-standard opportunity labels, not a multi-site clock-vs-solar full-day observational validation. Optimization is relative to artificial worlds and independent reference cost structure.
